settings.about: Brazilian Coffee House began in 1955 at Kuwait International Mill, roasting coffee for homes and cafés across the region. In 1995 the house arrived in Jordan, bringing the same craft of Turkish, filter, espresso, and specialty blends to Amman. Every tin still carries that mill heritage — slow, careful, and made to be shared.

coffee-culture-in-amman.title: Coffee culture in Amman
coffee-culture-in-amman.excerpt: From the cezve on the stove to the office espresso — how Jordan drinks coffee now.

category.name: Journal
category.description: Coffee culture from the house mill.

coffee-culture-in-amman.content:
Amman drinks coffee in layers. There is the morning cezve, cardamom rising through the kitchen. There is the office machine, the visit to a parent’s house, the tin opened for guests.

Brazilian Coffee House has been part of that rhythm since 1995, after decades of roasting at Kuwait International Mill. The blends are familiar on purpose: Turkish, filter, espresso, and the sachets people keep in a drawer for unexpected company.

how-we-make-turkish-coffee.title: How we make Turkish coffee
how-we-make-turkish-coffee.excerpt: A short guide to the house Turkish roast, the grind, and a calm cezve.

category.name: Journal
category.description: Coffee culture from the house mill.

how-we-make-turkish-coffee.content:
Turkish coffee is not hurried. Use a fine grind, cold water, and a cezve that can sit on a low flame. Sweeten in the pot if you take sugar. Add cardamom if you want the house cup.

Our light, medium, and dark Turkish tins are roasted for that method — not for a machine, not for a filter. Bring it just to the rise, pour, and wait for the grounds to settle.

from-the-mill-to-jordan.title: From the mill to Jordan
from-the-mill-to-jordan.excerpt: A heritage note: 1955 at Kuwait International Mill, 1995 in Jordan.

category.name: Journal
category.description: Coffee culture from the house mill.

from-the-mill-to-jordan.content:
The house began in 1955 at Kuwait International Mill. Forty years later the same roasting craft arrived in Jordan. The tins changed, the cities changed, the mill memory did not.

That is the story we still tell in the shop: origin lots and flavored Turkish, espresso for the machine, filter for the weekend, and Rio House for the cupboard that has to work on a busy morning.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.content: Brazilian Coffee House collects only what we need to fulfil orders, answer enquiries, and improve the shop. We do not sell personal data. Contact info@bch-coffee.com with privacy requests.

terms.title: Terms of Sale
terms.content: Orders are an offer to purchase. Cash on delivery orders are confirmed by our team. Prices are in Jordanian dinars. Demonstration catalogue prices may be edited in the admin.

shipping.title: Shipping
shipping.content: We deliver in Amman. Delivery is JD 2.000, free over JD 25.000. Lead times are confirmed after the order is placed. Remote areas may require a phone confirmation.

returns.title: Returns
returns.content: Unopened tins and sealed goods may be returned within 7 days if unused. Perishable opened coffee is not returnable. Write to info@bch-coffee.com to start a return.
